lines.text: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md inside:|a name, a description, and instructions.
lines.say: A skill is a folder with a skill dot M D inside: a name, a description, and instructions.

lines.text: It can carry scripts and reference files too.
Skills follow an open standard,|so Claude Code and Codex read the same format.
At the start, only each skill's name and description are in context.
When a task matches the description, or you type its slash name,|the full instructions load.
Scripts and reference files load only when the instructions need them,|so a long list of skills costs little until one is used.
These clips were built with a video skill.
It carried rules that weren't obvious:|the first frame becomes the thumbnail, and text under twenty-eight pixels gets flagged.
None of that was in a prompt.|The skill loaded it when the task needed it.
It also knew how to check and render each clip,|so that part never needed explaining.
The description is the trigger,|so write it as "Use when" and the situation.
Every description costs context on every request, so keep them short.
If a personal skill and a project skill share a name, the personal one wins.
When you paste the same playbook a third time, make it a skill.
A long procedure can run in its own subagent,|so it doesn't flood your conversation.
Codex reads skills from .agents/skills,|and you call one by typing a dollar sign and its name.
lines.say: Codex reads skills from dot agents slash skills, and you call one by typing a dollar sign and its name.
